name: Google Cloud TPU Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI)
version: v4 through v6e generations, per-chip figures
bandwidth_basis: PER CHIP, PER DIRECTION, v5e GENERATION AS THE REFERENCE POINT. Google's per-chip spec tables publish ICI bandwidth as a BIDIRECTIONAL aggregate per chip, so this record's typed value is one generation's per-direction half and the per-generation figures are all carried explicitly here: v5e publishes 'Bidirectional inter-chip interconnect (ICI) bandwidth (per chip) 400 GBps' across 4 ICI ports, giving the recorded 200 GB/s per direction; v6e publishes 800 GBps bidirectional across the same 4 ports, giving 400 GB/s per direction; v5p publishes 1200 GBps bidirectional per chip. v4 is NOT recorded as a number: Google's v4 docs give a link count ('Six interconnect links per chip') and topology but no per-chip ICI bandwidth figure, so v4's value is deliberately absent rather than inferred from another generation. Do not compare these per-chip numbers directly against nvlink-4 or amd-xgmi without checking direction - NVIDIA's per-GPU NVLink figures are bidirectional aggregates too, which is why nvswitch-4 records 450 GB/s per direction from a published 900 GB/s.
topology: Switched mesh, NOT a full mesh, and this is the defining difference from the GPU scale-up fabrics. Per generation: v4 uses a 3D mesh that can be reconfigured into a 3D torus, with 6 interconnect links per chip, a 4096-chip pod, and optical circuit switches between cubes - the v4 architecture paper is the source for the optical switching. v5p uses a 3D torus. v5e and v6e both use a 2D TORUS across a 256-chip pod. Google's pod-level docs give the consequences directly as published numbers, which is why those are worth reading instead of deriving a mesh diameter: v5e all-reduce 51.2 TB/s per pod against a BISECTION bandwidth of only 1.6 TB/s; v6e all-reduce 102.4 TB/s against bisection 3.2 TB/s. That ratio is the whole story of ICI versus NVSwitch - a torus gives strong nearest-neighbour and all-reduce performance at a bisection bandwidth roughly 30x lower than the all-reduce figure, whereas nvswitch-4's 8-GPU domain is non-blocking.
switching: The fabric is packet-switched with topology awareness, and Google publishes the bisection and all-reduce bandwidths separately precisely because they diverge so much. Beyond the pod, scaling is by POD and then by data-centre network, not by extending ICI: v5e/v6e publish 2x100 Gbps and 4x200 Gbps per-host NIC configurations respectively, with 6.4 TB/s and 25.6 TB/s of data-centre network bandwidth per pod. Note that for TPU the 'scale-up' and 'scale-out' boundary sits at the pod, unlike the GPU parts in this repo where it sits at the 8-GPU NVSwitch domain - a 4096-chip v4 pod is ONE scale-up domain, and the practical consequence is that TPU topology is fixed at slice granularity by how the slice is carved, which is a different engineering constraint from choosing a tensor-parallel degree.
notes: The scale-up fabric for every Google TPU in this repo, and the clearest example in the knowledge base of why a torus is not a mesh. PER-GENERATION PUBLISHED ICI FIGURES (all from Google's own per-chip spec tables): v4 - 6 links per chip, 3D mesh reconfigurable to 3D torus, 4096-chip pod, optical circuit switches between cubes, NO per-chip bandwidth published; v5p - 3D torus, 1200 GBps bidirectional per chip; v5e - 2D torus, 400 GBps bidirectional per chip over 4 ports, 256-chip pod, all-reduce 51.2 TB/s vs bisection 1.6 TB/s; v6e - 2D torus, 800 GBps bidirectional per chip over 4 ports, 256-chip pod, all-reduce 102.4 TB/s vs bisection 3.2 TB/s, plus 4x200 Gbps per-host NICs and 25.6 TB/s DC network per pod. INFERENCE CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this belongs in a memory-bound study: a torus deliberately trades bisection bandwidth for cheap nearest-neighbour links, and collectives are shaped around that. Ring and torus-aware algorithms are what the topology wants, and a naive flat all-reduce pays for the wraps. For a 2D torus the wrap-around edges are the expensive ones, so the standard mitigation is to arrange the tensor-parallel group to match the chip arrangement rather than to treat the pod as an unordered set of 256 equivalent devices. The 32x gap between v5e's all-reduce (51.2 TB/s) and bisection (1.6 TB/s) is the concrete number to reason from. COMPARE: amd-xgmi and amd-infinity-fabric-link get a fully connected 8-way domain with no wraps, so on an 8-GPU AMD node there is no torus penalty at all - AMD wins at small TP degree and loses at large pod scale, which is the same conclusion NVIDIA reaches from the other direction with a 72-GPU non-blocking NVSwitch domain. Note also that Google's own docs separate BF16/INT8 doubling behaviour across generations (v4 does NOT double INT8 over BF16, v5p's FP8 row is contested, v6e does double) - that is a compute-side inconsistency and must not be smuggled into a bandwidth comparison. KIND: filed as 'other' because ICI is a proprietary vendor fabric with no entry in the schema's interconnect enum, and it is not a member of any of the named families (not NVLink, not Ethernet, not InfiniBand) despite doing a scale-up job analogous to NVSwitch.
